paper_metadata.title: High density deformation nanotwins induced large plasticity improvement in polycrystalline γ-TiAl based intermetallic

evidence.quote: High density deformation nanotwins induced large plasticity improvement in polycrystalline γ-TiAl based intermetallic
this research realizes high compressive strength and plasticity simultaneously at room temperature in a Cr-rich γ-TiAl based alloy by introducing high density deformation nanotwins.

High density deformation nanotwins were exactly generated in massive γ phase during compression, the average density and width of these nanotwins can reach 3.07 ×107 m -1 and 13.78 nm, respectively (Figure 4a).
The local density and width of the nanotwins in γ lamellae can be measured as 1.54 ×108 m -1 and 5.74 nm in average from HRTEM images

High density deformation nanotwins can not only restrict the motion of dislocations, but also provide plenty of space for storing and the motion of dislocations, and thereby obviously improve the work hardening capacity of the as-annealed alloys.
the substantial improvement of compressive strength and fracture strain of as-annealed alloys mainly results from their excellent work-hardening abilities.

the generation of substantial Shockley partial dislocations and stacking faults during annealing could significantly reduce the nucleation energy barrier for deformation twins, which made high density deformation nanotwins generated in as-annealed alloys, especially in the γ lamellae.
